pr.title: ci(deep_gemm): keep DeepGEMM JIT error messages instead of exiting the process
pr.body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

This PR keeps native DeepGEMM JIT error messages so they reach the test report and the CI job trace. It does not change kernel behavior and does not fix any particular test failure.

**Why:** DeepGEMM's `CHECK_CUDA` and `CHECK_NVRTC` macros called `exit(1)` when a CUDA driver or NVRTC call failed. That ends the Python process before pytest writes its JUnit XML. The error message goes only to the per-batch log, and the sharding runner can report only that the XML is missing. H100/cu129 nightlies from 10/22 to 10/25 showed this, `cause=pytest did not produce JUnit XML`, for batches in three files that use the SM90 DeepGEMM JIT:

- `tests/gemm/test_fp8_blockscale_gemm.py`
- `tests/moe/test_unified_moe_cutlass.py`
- `tests/moe/test_unified_moe_fuzz.py`

We don't know what actually failed in those runs, and this PR doesn't try to find out. It makes sure that when something like this happens, the actual error is kept and reported.

**Changes:**

- **`deep_gemm/jit_utils.cuh`:** `CHECK_CUDA` and `CHECK_NVRTC` throw `std::runtime_error` instead of calling `exit(1)`. The message gives the error text, the failing call, and the file and line. TVM-FFI turns it into a Python `RuntimeError` on the test that hit it, so pytest finishes and records the error in the JUnit XML.
- **`deep_gemm/compiler.cuh`:** checks nvcc's exit status and that the kernel file exists. nvcc's error output is captured and included in the error message. Before this, a failed compile only showed up later, when loading the missing kernel file failed.
- **`deep_gemm/runtime.cuh`:** loading a missing or empty kernel file raises an error that names the path. `~Runtime` no longer throws.
- **`scripts/infra/test_sharding/workers.py`:**
  - When a pytest batch exits without writing JUnit XML, the message gives the exit code and the full ID of the last test that started. That is kept after the test finishes, so a pytest that exits during teardown, after its last test reported, still names it. The timeout message still names the test that was running.
  - The runner prints the last 40 lines of the batch log into the job trace, so the error is visible even when the batch log artifact isn't kept. It also prints the log tail when pytest exits with an infrastructure error code, and when reading pytest's output fails (it prints what is already in the log without waiting for more).
  - The batch log is appended to across executions of the same batch. The tail starts no earlier than where this execution's output begins, so it cannot show output from an earlier run. It reads at most 16 KB.
  - Batches with no XML are still reported as infrastructure failures, never as passing.
  - Batch pytest runs with `--capture=tee-sys` and `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1` (unless already set). pytest's default capture holds a test's output until the test reports, so a test that ends the process lost the error it printed, and the log tail showed only pytest's header. With `tee-sys`, Python output goes to the batch log as it is printed and is still attached to failure reports. `PYTHONUNBUFFERED` keeps `os._exit()` and a native `exit()` from dropping buffered stdout. Trade-off: output that native code writes straight to the file descriptors now appears inline in the batch log instead of the report's "Captured ..." sections. Neither was in the JUnit XML, since `junit_logging` is not set.
- **`tests/infra/test_sharding/test_workers.py`:** regression tests with a fake pytest:
  - It prints an error and exits with code 1 without writing XML. The batch is reported as an infrastructure failure with the exit code and last test, no XML is promoted, and the log tail containing the error appears on the console.
  - It exits after its only test finished; the message still names that test.
  - Its log already holds output from an earlier execution; the tail shows only this execution's output, and the earlier output stays in the file.
  - Its output fails to parse; the reader-failure message is kept and the log tail is printed.
  - A unit test checks that finishing a test clears the running test but keeps the last-started one.

  Two tests run real pytest, since the fake pytest above prints directly and cannot show capture behavior:

  - A test prints to stdout, stderr and file descriptor 2, then calls `os._exit(1)`. All three lines appear in the console log tail. This fails without the capture change, and also with `tee-sys` alone, without `PYTHONUNBUFFERED`.
  - A failing test's output still appears under "Captured stdout call" in its report.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Motivating report: GitLab `dl/flashinfer/flashinfer-ci` scheduled unit-test nightlies from 10/22 to 10/25. Example jobs: 502615440, 502615451, 508255535, 508255548.
Audit marker: `flashinfer-gitlab-nightly-20261022-20261025-pytest-missing-junit-v1`

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues. All hooks passed with no changes; the broken-symlink check had no files to check.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).
- [ ] This PR requires **full-scope** CI, not targeted tests (expensive; justify below).

Targeted H100 run (cu129, before the rebase, when the tests were still under `tests/test_sharding`) for `tests/gemm/test_fp8_blockscale_gemm.py tests/moe/test_unified_moe_cutlass.py tests/moe/test_unified_moe_fuzz.py tests/test_sharding`: 1,074 tests, 811 passed, 0 failed, 263 skipped. Every batch wrote JUnit XML. The DeepGEMM path compiles and passes on H100 with the new error handling. This run did not hit a DeepGEMM error, so the new error path was exercised by the regression test, not by a real GPU failure.

Rebased onto `main` (25bc267eb), which moved the sharding runner and its tests to `scripts/infra/` and `tests/infra/` (#8993). Locally, `tests/infra/test_sharding/test_workers.py` passes on this branch (18 passed; the four tests added for the review fixes fail against the previous `workers.py`, and the real-pytest exit test fails without the capture change) and pre-commit passes on the changed files. `tests/infra/test_sharding/test_test_path_scope.py::test_sm107_runner_selects_supported_lanes` currently fails on `main`; that is unrelated to this PR and left to the test's owners, so a CI scope that includes all of `tests/infra/test_sharding` will show those failures until it is fixed. The H100 results above are from before this rebase.

Demo in CI (draft #9724, do not merge): this branch plus a CPU test that prints a fake CUDA error and calls `os._exit(1)`.

- [Before the capture change](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/actions/runs/44552016993/job/135658408079): the batch was reported with the exit code and test name, but the log tail ended at pytest's header, without the error.
- [After](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/actions/runs/44778877817/job/136436289928): the tail shows both the stdout and stderr lines the test printed before exiting. The other 11,417 `tests/cpu` tests passed, and the 3 demo tests stayed pending rather than passing. The targeted H100 lane ran `tests/infra/test_sharding/test_workers.py`: 18 of 18 passed.

Locally (no GPU), the changed DeepGEMM headers compile on the host side with clang `-Wall`. A small program that triggers both macros gets an exception with the expected message instead of `exit(1)`.

Suggested CI test targets: `tests/gemm/test_fp8_blockscale_gemm.py tests/moe/test_unified_moe_cutlass.py tests/moe/test_unified_moe_fuzz.py tests/infra/test_sharding/test_workers.py`
